meta.status: first tranche + 5 showcase adoptions (2026-08-09). Not complete.

conceptNameSources.mathcat: Name taken verbatim from MathCAT Rules/Intent/*.yaml. Best available proxy for the eventual W3C open vocabulary, since MathCAT is the reference implementation. PREFER THESE.
conceptNameSources.w3c: Name taken from W3C open/core vocabulary material.
conceptNameSources.coined: Our own name. Expect to rename when the W3C vocabulary settles.

mathcatField.infers: MathCAT already gets this right unaided. Value of annotating is SRE-only. Tier 2.
mathcatField.wrong: MathCAT infers something, but often the wrong thing. Annotating fixes BOTH channels. Tier 1.
mathcatField.absent: MathCAT has no rule. Annotating fixes both channels. Tier 1.

notes: arity is informational. Actual arity is counted from the \iarg markers at parse time, so one entry serves whatever notation uses it.
macro.name must not duplicate another entry's macro.name — build-time error.
macro.name MAY shadow a package command (physics, ams, base): verified that config macros win in either load order. An author's own \newcommand still beats ours, which is correct.
confidence flags an entry a subject-matter expert should review before use.

groups.core-authored: The hand-authored core (34 as of 2026-08-09). Always enabled; toggles cannot turn it off.
groups.physics-quantum: Physics incl. bra-ket / quantum notation beyond the core.
groups.other: Everything the rollup map does not otherwise place.

meta.groupNotes: Rollup groups are the toggle surface (build-time flag and per-document intent-groups: metadata). Entries may also carry a fine-grained "area" (from the open-list importer) and "experimental": true. "mathcatName" records MathCAT's divergent name for the same concept where one exists (see docs/mathcat-vs-open-list-comparison.md); the build MATHCAT_NAMES switch selects which name the intent attribute carries.

notations.mathcatBehaviour: determinant if the content is an <mi> of only uppercase letters, else absolute-value. Controlled by ClearSpeak_AbsoluteValue (Auto | AbsEnd | Cardinality | Determinant); default Auto.
notations.priority: highest — |S| for set cardinality is read as 'determinant of S'

notations.description: one expression between double vertical bars
notations.priority: low — MathCAT is right; SRE says 'the metric of'
high — genuinely undecidable without the author; the canonical W3C example

notations.description: two comma-separated expressions in square brackets
angle brackets with an internal vertical bar
notations.priority: highest for physics — SRE reads the bar as the relation 'divides'

notations.description: ket followed by bra: |a><b| outer product / projector
notations.priority: high for physics/QC — equal labels = projector; physics \ketbra \outerproduct \dyad \op all produce it; starred variants emit a FLAT token run (no wrapper mrow, non-stretchy bars)

notations.description: angle brackets with two internal vertical bars: matrix-element sandwich
notations.mathcatBehaviour: absent — SRE reads both bars as 'divides'; starred physics variants misread as absolute value
notations.priority: high for physics — <psi|A|psi> with equal labels is the expectation-value reading (author chooses); physics \mel \matrixelement and 2-arg \expval produce it

notations.description: a bar over one or more symbols
notations.mathcatBehaviour: infers line-segment or repeating-decimal depending on content

notations.description: a capital T in the exponent position

concepts.notes: Shadows physics \abs, deliberately. Same meaning, but ours emits intent.
MathCAT infers this for an uppercase <mi>. Annotating still helps SRE, and removes reliance on a typographic guess.
HIGHEST VALUE ENTRY. |S| for a set is read by MathCAT as 'determinant of S' because S is uppercase. Ubiquitous in discrete maths and set theory.
MathCAT has a vector-magnitude rule but |v| lowercase falls through to absolute-value. Review: is 'magnitude' or 'absolute value' wanted for vectors in your courses?
Complex modulus. REVIEW: many courses simply say 'absolute value' for this; may be redundant with absolute-value. Also collides conceptually with modular arithmetic 'mod'.
Shadows physics \norm, deliberately. SRE alone says 'the metric of', which is wrong.
REVIEW argument order: phrasing wants the subscript first ('the L 2 norm of v'), so slot a is the subscript. Verify this reads correctly.
MathCAT reads (a,b) as an open interval. Wrong whenever it is a point or a tuple — very common in coordinate geometry.
Only ambiguous in the bare (a,b) form used in number theory. With an explicit \gcd both engines are fine, so the macro spells it out.
MathCAT calls this 'binomial'. REVIEW which spelling to keep; W3C material uses binomial-coefficient. MathCAT names this concept "binomial" (defs:19, "choose"); recorded per the mathcatName policy.
physics has \ip / \innerproduct; ours is named ipof to leave those alone since their bracket style differs.

DECIDED 2026-08-05 (docs/braket-intent-recommendations.md): distinct concept name, spoken as inner product. Evidence: 'inner product of X with Y' dominant across Susskind/Adams/Shor transcripts; #90 thread converged on distinct bra/ket names (Ginev endorsed; Böhm's final GitHub position). MathCAT channel speaks the name literally with comma separators: 'braket of a comma b' (verified live via NVDA 2026-08-05). Distinct from our inner-product entry (angle-comma notation). Fluent speech drops everything but labels ('phi psi') — noted, not implemented; terse layer later. Rename once W3C settles #90. physics owns \braket/\ip.

DECIDED 2026-08-05. Ket-first order: Wikipedia explicit ('pronounce it ket-A'), Zwiebach/Susskind transcripts, IBM-Watrous ('read as ket a'), German/French parallel; label-first 'psi ket' unattested anywhere. Fluent speech drops 'ket' ('the state psi') — noted, not implemented. No macro — physics owns \ket.
DECIDED 2026-08-05. 'bra vector psi' attested ~8x (Susskind); IBM-Watrous 'read as bra a'. Medium not high: no other transcript voicing found; bras rarely voiced standalone. physics owns \bra.

W3C open list has this exact name+notation (arity 1, 'expectation value of $1', area quantum physics). Arity here is informational: authored with a second \iarg (the \expval{A}{psi} form, <psi|A|psi>), mid1 engages: 'the expectation value of A in the state psi' — verbatim instructor-endorsed (Adams 8.04 L4, answering a pronunciation question). Fluent alternative 'psi A psi' noted, not implemented. Distinct from probability's expected-value E(X). physics owns \expval/\ev.

DECIDED 2026-08-05. |psi><phi|. Spoken as outer product: Susskind 'the outer product of the ket vector B with the bra vector A'; Azure 'the ketbra or outer product'. 'dyad' is attested second choice (Susskind), not used. Equal-labels case is a projector ('projector onto psi') — future enhancement, noted. MathCAT literal fallback: 'ketbra of a comma b' (verified live 2026-08-05). Distinct from W3C outer-product (X⊗Y infix). physics owns \ketbra/\outerproduct/\dyad/\op.

DECIDED 2026-08-05. <m|A|n>, args in written order (bra label, operator, ket label) -> 'the matrix element m A n'. Evidence: Susskind names it 'matrix element of K between vector B and vector A' and fluently reads bare 'n K r'; corpus supports 'matrix element of A between states m and n'. Rejected reordering template ('of $2 between $1 and $3') — moves args away from notation and every attested reading. Equal-labels case = expectation value (author's choice which intent fits). Within #90's 'maybe others'. physics owns \mel/\matrixelement.
MathCAT infers line-segment for an overline over two capitals, so complex conjugate of AB is misread. The canonical W3C example of this ambiguity.
x-bar in statistics. REVIEW spoken form: 'x bar' is what many statistics courses actually say aloud.
REVIEW: arity here is 1 with the name spoken after the phrase, giving 'the vector v'. Confirm that reads naturally.
MathCAT has calculus rules for nabla forms but not for d/dx. REVIEW against MathCAT Rules/Intent/calculus.yaml before finalising.
Four macro arguments but arity 3: the differential variable #4 is presentational only and is not an intent slot. REVIEW whether it should be.

Tier 3: BOTH engines already handle set-builder well — verified that '\left\{ x \mid x>0 \right\}' speaks as 'the set of all x such that x is greater than 0' with no annotation. The macro exists mainly to occupy the name so braket cannot autoload.
PLACEHOLDER. Probably redundant with cardinality; included only to record that the case was considered. Delete unless a reviewer wants it.

Newton dot, \dot{x}. Authored 2026-08-09 for the showcase/platform demo (APMTH 108 / Strogatz). Coined per the 5.7 shortcut: open list has no entry; check W3C discussion before promoting. No macro: wrap \dot{...} explicitly.

x^* as equilibrium of a dynamical system (APMTH 108 / Strogatz). Same notation means optimal-solution in optimization — the star is course-dependent; suggest tool must offer both. Authored 2026-08-09, coined per 5.7 shortcut.
x^* as the optimizer (APMTH 121 / LP, Chvatal). Counterpart of fixed-point on the same notation. Authored 2026-08-09, coined per 5.7 shortcut.
\nabla f. Open list has NO gradient entry (verified 2026-08-09); nabla is also divergence/curl/covariant-derivative depending on context, so no macro — wrap explicitly. Coined per 5.7 shortcut.
